small_guidance:
- Fuse the softmax into the matmul epilogue when BLOCK_N == N (i.e. tile spans the whole row): with BLOCK_N=8192 the row fits, but tiling N requires a separate softmax. Try a persistent matmul where each program owns a full row tile (BLOCK_M rows × full N) using a K-loop with split accumulators, then do max/exp/sum in registers and store normalized output — eliminates the softmax read/write of the 1024×8192 tensor (~32MB).
- Add larger-N autotune configs (BLOCK_N=128/256 with BLOCK_K=128, num_stages=4) and try BLOCK_M=64,BLOCK_N=128,BLOCK_K=128 num_warps=4 stages=4 — K=8192 is large so deeper pipelining of the K loop should help on 4090.
- For the standalone softmax, BLOCK_N=8192 with num_warps=16 is excessive on Ada (max 8 warps useful per CTA on 4090); drop to num_warps=8 and num_stages=2, and consider a two-pass online softmax with BLOCK_N=2048 to reduce register pressure.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a fused matmul→GELU→softmax kernel where each program processes a full output row (or small group of rows). Since N=8192 fits in shared/registers across a CTA, accumulate the full row by looping over K in BLOCK_K chunks against tiles of B, apply GELU on the accumulator, then do an in-register row max + exp + sum + normalize before storing. This removes the intermediate 32MB GELU tensor traffic entirely.
- Alternatively, split-K matmul writing to a scratch then a fused gelu+softmax pass — but the fully-fused single-pass row-wise GEMM is preferred since M=1024 gives enough parallelism (1024 rows / BLOCK_M tiles → plenty of CTAs on 128 SMs).
- Pre-transpose the weight once in __init__ (store W^T contiguous) so the inner B loads in the GEMM are along the contiguous axis without relying on stride swap, improving L2 reuse and enabling vectorized 128-bit loads.
